extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard contract specialists, COTRs, contracting officers, program managers, and policymakers responsible for A-76 and other service contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating performance, cost changes, administration, and documentation for Coast Guard A-76 (commercial activity) service contracts, including comparisons to the government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) and application of wage/price adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison to MEO ('should cost')
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the actual contract cost with the original contract cost and the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) using OMB Circular A-76 guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEO costs computed using current standard Government GS and military pay scales with annual inflation and retirement factors from OMB; obtain actual and original contract costs from contract file and COMDT cost comparisons; use comparisons to determine if activity is operating at a savings to the Government (examples and tables provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: 10% personnel-cost savings threshold for award
rubrics_metrics.description: Award decisions should ensure the contract is lower than the Government MEO by 10% or greater of MEO personnel cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes contracts were initially awarded because they were lower than MEO by 10%+; if the bid is less than the 10% personnel-cost increment (example: 5.4%), the contract should not have been awarded. Use this threshold when judging award validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recompute/revise MEO when contract scope or conditions change
rubrics_metrics.description: When the scope of a contract changes (e.g., reduced coverage) or contract conditions change, the MEO must be recomputed to ensure savings are still realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Support Center Seattle security MEO did not reflect reduced scope and therefore may not have accurately shown Government savings; policy should require revised MEO comparisons prior to award or renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely award process / avoidance of prolonged extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts should be awarded or reawarded in a timely manner to avoid repeated extensions after the final option year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report observed delays from 1.5 months to one year after end of final option year; causes include slow specification review/approvals, long negotiation prep, long DCAA audit lead times, and heavy contract specialist workload. Frequent extensions are flagged as a management problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete, self-contained contract file documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract files must fully document actions taken, obligations made, modifications, and the rationale so they can stand alone for later review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contract administration transferred to MLCPAC many files were incomplete and could not explain actions taken; missing documentation impedes reconstruction of decisions (e.g., obligations, deobligations, negotiated prices). Ensure post-negotiation memoranda, obligations, and modifications are recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and adequacy of contractor QA plan and government QA surveillance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the contractor's Quality Assurance (QA) plan and the Government's QA surveillance plan must exist and be adequate to monitor and administer the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report states these plans are essential; absence made it difficult to properly justify performance deductions and monitor contract performance. Government and contractor plans should be completed promptly and used to justify deductions and surveillance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of COTR assignment and training
rubrics_metrics.description: COTRs should be assigned with appropriate duration and receive training that covers day‑to‑day duties and QA methods applicable to their specific contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although most COTRs received basic COTR/QA training, courses often provided little practical guidance for daily COTR duties; COTRs reported training did not adequately address QA paperwork requirements or lessons learned. Assign experienced COTRs and provide targeted training and assistance in developing surveillance plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor staffing qualifications and compliance with specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor must recruit, hire, and retain fully qualified personnel as required by contract specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low wage rates led to high turnover and hiring unqualified personnel (hired 'off the street'), which violated contract specifications and contributed to marginal performance. Wage levels, staffing plans, and training obligations should be evaluated during performance reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Manager (PM) qualifications, leadership, and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor's PM should have relevant experience, leadership, and communication skills; continuity of a motivated prior-service PM can improve contract success and smooth transitions between contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: hiring a motivated prior-service SS as PM improved operations; poor leadership and weak communication by PM contributed to marginal performance. Evaluate PM background and consider continuity when contractors change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely application and accuracy of wage determinations and economic price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: DOL wage determinations and economic price adjustments (e.g., food price increases) must be applied accurately and in a timely manner; contractors should have opportunity to request adjustments when justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays in applying wage increases caused contractor difficulties; inaccurate or low DOL determinations (not questioned before solicitation) can cause long-term cost increases. Track DOL determinations and ensure correct economic adjustments are processed promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and adjustment of Headquarters funding based on contract cost changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Headquarters funding allocations, which may be based on initial negotiated contract prices, should be monitored and adjusted when contract costs increase or decrease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report found initial award cost used as funding base and funding levels were not changed as contract costs varied; monitoring is needed to reflect current contract costs across budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and justification of contract modifications and deobligations
rubrics_metrics.description: All contract modifications (including those due to continuing resolutions) and deobligations must be recorded with reasons and reflected in contract totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables of modifications should be maintained; deobligations when usage is below estimates (e.g., fewer meals sold) must be documented. Missing records (e.g., undocumented deobligations) were observed and hindered cost reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of initial workload/usage estimates used in pricing (e.g., meals sold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial estimates of workload or usage (such as number of meals sold) used to set contract prices must be accurate or periodically re-evaluated, because actual usage affects deobligations and contract cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declining meals sold offset some cost increases via deobligations; inaccurate original estimates should prompt closer inspection and may invalidate award decisions if they materially change cost comparisons to MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance monitoring and enforcement with actionable QA metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance should be actively monitored and enforcement actions (deductions) must be supported by QA surveillance data and clear metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deductions were taken for sleeping on patrol and falsifying logs but were hard to justify without a QA surveillance plan. QA systems should provide clear standards and records to support deductions and corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning solicitation assumptions (e.g., wage determinations) before award
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation assumptions such as DOL wage determinations and other inputs should be validated and questioned prior to release of solicitation to avoid inaccurate baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Support Center Alameda's solicitation used a wage determination believed to be low and inaccurate and was not questioned; this contributed to contract costs approaching or exceeding MEO. Validate key assumptions pre-solicitation.
